method: No UN volume exists for 2023. Volume = fall in official North Kivu output, 1,120 (2020-22 mean) - 605 = 515 t. Pass-through 50/75/100% gives 257/386/515 t over 763 t. Rubaya was held by PARECO-FF/Wazalendo, not M23, until 30 Apr 2024.
falsifiers: Mine-level Rwandan production records showing the rise; independent grade or analytical-fingerprint tests tying Rwandan exports to Rwandan pits; a documented stock drawdown or a non-Kivu source (Burundi, Uganda, Maniema) of matching size; Rubaya output shown to leave by another route; official North Kivu output recovering without a fall in Rwandan exports.

method: Low: 120 t x 6 observed months x 50% = 360 t. Central: 120 t x 8 months x 75% = 720 t. High: 150 t x 8 months x 100% = 1,200 t, capped at 100%. All over 1044 t. Global Witness >=1,400 t in the first 12 months fits about 117 t/month.
falsifiers: Mine-level Rwandan production records showing the rise; independent grade or analytical-fingerprint tests tying Rwandan exports to Rwandan pits; a documented stock drawdown or a non-Kivu source (Burundi, Uganda, Maniema) of matching size; Rubaya output shown to leave by another route; official North Kivu output recovering without a fall in Rwandan exports.

method: Excess uses the frozen cassiterite baseline: 2,743 - 1,299 = 1,444 t. Low: 120 x 12 x 50% = 720 t. Central: (1,440 Rubaya + 175 half of South Kivu 2024) x 75% = 1,211 t. High: (150 x 12 + 175) x 100%, capped. On the BNR baseline (1,198 t) the shares are 60/100/100. On the unfrozen 627 t all are 100, and Rubaya alone would exceed the excess.
falsifiers: Mine-level Rwandan production records showing the rise; independent grade or analytical-fingerprint tests tying Rwandan exports to Rwandan pits; a documented stock drawdown or a non-Kivu source (Burundi, Uganda, Maniema) of matching size; Rubaya output shown to leave by another route; official North Kivu output recovering without a fall in Rwandan exports.

method: Volume = half of South Kivu (about 1,500 t, annex 26) plus North Kivu artisanal exports (486 t) = 1,986 t. Low: 1,500 x 50% = 750 t. Central: 1,986 x 75% = 1,490 t. High: 1,986 t. Half-of-South-Kivu applies only from Sept 2025, so the volume may be high for the year; official Kivu figures may be low for real output. Over the UN rise of 2,841 t. This keeps the low-value Cambodia tonnage in the denominator, so it understates the share of concentrate.
falsifiers: Evidence that the 2025 rise came from a named Rwandan mine or from stock; RMB or NISR production data; ITSCI or customs data tying the October 2025 spike (1,460 t) to non-DRC origins; evidence that official Kivu volumes moved through Kindu and Kalemie instead, as the ministry says part did.

Kivu loss (3,273 t) then exceeds the excess by about 2,053 t, so much of the lost Kivu ore went elsewhere or was not produced.

method: Comtrade excess 280 t vs 2022-24 mean; BNR to Nov suggests none, hence low = 0. Central: two-thirds of 200 t South Kivu = 133 t x 75% = 100 t. High: all 180 t of lost Kivu exports. Weak: Rwanda is a real tungsten producer.
falsifiers: Reconciling BNR with Comtrade for 2025 would settle whether any excess exists.
